evals.prompt: Our SAD for the 'MediRemind' medication-adherence platform defines a component called the Notification Service (SAD section 4.3, decided in ADR-007 'Use a queue-backed push architecture'). It must satisfy FRD-021 (patients receive a push reminder at each scheduled dose time), FRD-022 (a caregiver is notified if a dose is not confirmed within 30 minutes), and NFR-005 (reminder delivery within 60 seconds of schedule, 99.9% of the time). The team runs 2-week sprints with about 20 points of capacity and already has a standard team-wide Definition of Done. Break this component down into an Epic with sprint-ready Stories and Tasks so we can start pulling work next sprint.
evals.expected_output: One Epic titled after the Notification Service component with Architecture Link (SAD 4.3, ADR-007), Business Link, Success Criteria, and a Story list; each Story titled as a behavior with a narrative (or plain behavioral statement for system-to-system Stories), Given/When/Then acceptance criteria testable directly, traceability to this Epic and exactly one of FRD-021/FRD-022/NFR-005, an estimate, dependencies, and a Definition of Ready check; Tasks are concrete implementation steps under Stories with no acceptance criteria of their own.
expectations: The Epic is titled after the architecture component/capability (e.g. 'Notification Service'), not an activity like 'Build notification stuff'
The Epic includes an Architecture Link naming SAD section 4.3 and ADR-007, a Business Link, and explicit Success Criteria
Every Story traces to exactly one Epic and exactly one requirement ID (FRD-021, FRD-022, or NFR-005) — no orphaned or multi-requirement Stories
Story titles name behaviors (e.g. 'Send dose reminder push at scheduled time'), not tasks or technologies
User-facing Stories use the 'As a <actor>, I want <capability>, so that <benefit>' narrative; system-to-system Stories use a plain behavioral statement instead of a forced persona
Every Story has Given/When/Then (or checklist) acceptance criteria specific enough to write a test from directly — nothing like 'works correctly'
Every Story carries an estimate and identified dependencies, and each is sized to fit within one 2-week sprint (INVEST Small), with any larger candidate split
Tasks are concrete technical steps (migration, producer, tests) inside Stories, with estimates but no acceptance criteria of their own
Definition of Done is referenced as the inherited team standard, not rewritten per Story; each Story is checked against the Definition of Ready before being called sprint-eligible

evals.prompt: My manager forwarded me one line from a meeting: 'We need offline mode in the mobile app — break this down into stories for the team.' That's genuinely all I have. Can you produce the epic and the sprint-ready story breakdown?
evals.expected_output: A response that declines to fabricate a sprint-ready breakdown from a one-liner, and instead walks through the skill's Required Inputs — which SAD component/capability this maps to, which FRD/NFR requirement IDs each Story must satisfy, team capacity and sprint length, and existing DoR/DoD conventions — asking for them or clearly marking any sketch as a provisional draft that fails Definition of Ready until traceability and estimates exist.
expectations: The response does not present a fabricated breakdown as sprint-ready; any sketch is explicitly labeled provisional/not Ready
It asks which SAD component or capability 'offline mode' maps to (or flags that no architecture link exists yet)
It asks for the FRD/NFR requirement ID(s) involved, and does not invent requirement IDs to fill the traceability field
It flags that a Story that cannot name its Epic and requirement is scope without a design basis (the orphaned-Story problem)
It asks for team capacity and sprint length, since Stories cannot be sized to 'fits in one sprint' without them
It asks whether the team already has Definition of Ready / Definition of Done conventions rather than inventing new ones
It states explicitly that unestimated, untraceable stories fail the Definition of Ready and must not enter sprint planning

It notes that 'offline mode' is Epic-sized (too large to implement or estimate as one unit) and would need splitting via named patterns (e.g. workflow steps, happy path vs. edge cases) once inputs exist

evals.prompt:
Review this backlog extract for our 'ShopLite' e-commerce build before sprint planning tomorrow and list every problem:

EPIC E-9: Build checkout stuff
(no success criteria recorded)

STORY S-31: Update the database
- Estimate: 3 pts
- AC: none
- Epic: E-9

STORY S-32: Checkout flow
- As a shopper, I want to check out, so that I can buy things
- AC: checkout works correctly end to end
- Estimate: 21 pts (team velocity is 18/sprint; we figure it'll span 2-3 sprints, that's fine)
- Epic: E-9, Requirement: FRD-104
- DoD for this story: we agreed to skip code review and tests on this one to hit the date

STORY S-33: Send order confirmation email
- AC: Given a completed order, when payment settles, then a confirmation email with order number and line items is sent within 2 minutes
- Estimate: 3 pts
- Epic: (none) Requirement: (none)
evals.expected_output: A review that catches every planted defect: E-9 titled as an activity with no success criteria; S-31 is a Task disguised as a Story (no acceptance criteria, no independent value); S-32's acceptance criterion 'works correctly' is untestable, it is oversized at 21 points vs 18 velocity and must be split by a named pattern, and its per-Story weakened Definition of Done is illegitimate; S-33 is orphaned with no Epic or requirement link — each with the fix the skill prescribes.
expectations: Flags Epic E-9's title 'Build checkout stuff' as an activity, not a component/capability, and its missing success criteria (the epic-that-never-closes anti-pattern)
Flags S-31 'Update the database' as a Task disguised as a Story — no acceptance criteria, not independently valuable — to be reframed around a behavior or demoted to a Task inside a real Story
Flags S-32's acceptance criterion 'checkout works correctly end to end' as untestable and demands criteria specific enough to write a test from
Flags S-32 as oversized (21 pts against 18/sprint velocity, spanning multiple sprints) and rejects 'it'll span 2-3 sprints' — it fails INVEST Small and must be split
Recommends splitting S-32 along at least one named pattern from the skill (workflow steps, business rules, CRUD, happy path vs. edge cases, or cross-cutting concerns)
Flags S-32's per-Story Definition of Done ('skip code review and tests') as redefining the standing team DoD — the quality bar is team-wide, not negotiated per Story
Flags S-33 as an orphaned Story with no Epic and no FRD/NFR requirement link, despite having good acceptance criteria
Concludes with a Definition of Ready verdict: none of these Stories is sprint-eligible as written
